It's called Rayleigh scattering! Basically, the sun's light has to travel further through the atmosphere at sunset. The shorter blue wavelengths get scattered away, leaving the longer red and orange ones to reach your eyes. 🌅
Basically, because sunlight has to travel through more atmosphere when the sun is low. The shorter blue wavelengths get scattered away, leaving the longer red and orange ones to reach your eyes. 🌇

Basically, it's all about the distance. At sunset, sunlight has to travel through more of the atmosphere to reach you. The shorter blue wavelengths get scattered away, leaving the longer red and orange ones to make it through! 🌅

Basically, it's called Rayleigh scattering. Blue light scatters away more easily, so when the sun is low, the light has to travel further through the atmosphere. Only the longer wavelengths—the reds and oranges—make it through to your eyes. 🌅
